case_name: Sunil Kumar Puniya vs Smt. Sharda Puniya (Sahu)

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Sharda Puniya (Sahu), wife; Ku. Bhawya Puniya, daughter

facts_of_case: Marriage between applicant and respondent No.1 in 2018. Applicant misbehaved with respondent No.1, assaulted her, and pushed her out of their residential house. Respondent No.1 filed application under Section 125 of CrPC for grant of maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized in violation of Section 5(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act is null and void.
legal_principles.held: The respondent No.1 has willfully and intentionally hidden the fact of earlier marriage in the application filed under Section 125 of CrPC for grant of maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: A person who has already married another person cannot solemnize a subsequent marriage without obtaining a decree of divorce from the competent Court.
legal_principles.held: The respondent No.1 has not obtained a decree of divorce from the competent Court before solemnizing her second marriage with the applicant.

legal_principles.principle: A person who has not obtained a decree of divorce from the competent Court before solemnizing a subsequent marriage is not entitled to maintenance from the new spouse.
legal_principles.held: The respondent No.1 is not entitled for interim maintenance from the applicant as she has already married another person and without obtaining a decree of divorce, solemnized her second marriage with the applicant.

legal_principles.principle: A person who has concealed the fact of earlier marriage in an application for maintenance is not entitled to that relief.
legal_principles.held: The respondent No.1 has willfully and intentionally hidden the fact of earlier marriage in the application filed under Section 125 of CrPC for grant of maintenance.

outcome.final_order: Order dated 24.10.2024, passed by learned Principal judge, Family Court, Raipur, set aside and the order granting maintenance amount of Rs. 15,000/- to respondents was modified.
